investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-28T23:19–23:26Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod could not be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence at all—leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and both contract assertions unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. No preemption victims were available, so every new remote-agent pod remained Unschedulable for the full 143-second observation window. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never started, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was written, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259 to be fully unmet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible peer-pod nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Supported by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling messages.

SECONDARY — peer-pod node count is insufficient for the current workload demand: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if those nodes are sized for a small number of concurrent VMs, any spike in remote-agent creation will exhaust capacity quickly.

TERTIARY — node affinity or selector misconfiguration on the pod spec: 4 nodes did not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or were recently changed, this could artificially shrink the eligible node set.

QUATERNARY — a stuck or leaked remote-agent VM from a prior eval run is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., affinity misconfiguration) is primary.

If the 4 non-peer-pod nodes are shown to have been incorrectly excluded by a recently changed node affinity rule (and fixing the affinity allows scheduling without adding VM capacity), then affinity misconfiguration is the primary cause rather than capacity exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If no existing pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of failure, the resource accounting or node labeling may be incorrect rather than the capacity being genuinely consumed.
If only remote-agent-create failed and remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passed, the shared-dependency hypothesis would be weakened and a check-specific code path would need investigation.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm label are in Ready state, alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider a canary eval that attempts remote-agent creation with a short timeout (e.g., 30s) and reports a WARN rather than FAIL on scheduling delays, distinguishing transient capacity pressure from sustained exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-28T23:21–23:26Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable nodes for new kata peer-pod VMs — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent(..., "remote", ...) as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), no agent pod was ever scheduled, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With preemption also unable to free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner cannot create a remote agent pod, so it never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an eval-detected signal of a production infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist.

[Likely secondary] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peer-pod capable nodes), and those 2 are already at capacity. A reduction in the number of kata-capable nodes (e.g., a node being cordoned, drained, or removed) would shrink the schedulable pool.
[Possible] A surge in concurrent remote-agent usage or a prior eval run that did not clean up its agent pods may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving none for the observability probe.

[Possible but unconfirmed] A cluster configuration change (node pool resize, resource quota reduction, or label/taint change) that reduced kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity or narrowed node affinity eligibility. No suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so this remains a hypothesis requiring cluster audit.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-28T23:19–23:26Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod could not be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence at all—leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and both contract assertions unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. No preemption victims were available, so every new remote-agent pod remained Unschedulable for the full 143-second observation window. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: because the pod never started, the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was written, causing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259 to be fully unmet.

Supported by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling messages.

SECONDARY — peer-pod node count is insufficient for the current workload demand: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if those nodes are sized for a small number of concurrent VMs, any spike in remote-agent creation will exhaust capacity quickly.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are NOT exhausted (i.e., allocatable > used) on the 2 kata-capable nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the scheduler message would need a different explanation (e.g., a quota or admission webhook rejection).

If a subsequent eval run passes (all four evidence keys present) without any cluster changes, it would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' are found to actually carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label, the node affinity/selector on the pod spec may be misconfigured rather than the resource being exhausted.
If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime passed, the failure would be localized to the state-polling step rather than the shared pod scheduling layer.
If the cluster has more than 6 nodes or the node count changed between the eval run and the investigation, the '0/6 nodes' count in the message may not reflect current cluster state.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on each node in the production cluster and warns before full exhaustion (e.g., warn at 80% utilization, fail at 100%).
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) that are still Running or Pending, alerting before they exhaust the VM slot pool.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector/affinity is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes), catching pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider adding a pre-flight check in the remote-agent-state runner branch (run-status-probes.mjs) that queries cluster capacity before attempting createAgent and returns a more actionable SKIP or WARN status with capacity details when slots are unavailable, rather than waiting 143s for the scheduler timeout.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-28T23:24–23:26Z with the identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent, and consequently zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream checks to fail with empty evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval environment's production-api Kubernetes cluster. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to real end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls requireOrgId() then createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) — both calls require a live agent pod, which the scheduler cannot provide.
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the most strongly supported cause. The scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on exactly 2 nodes, and preemption found no victims, indicating all vm slots are occupied by running workloads.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes). The other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity.

Cluster under-provisioning for peak load: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource; if concurrent remote-agent workloads (from users or other eval runs) consumed all slots before the eval pod was submitted, the eval would be blocked.

Eval runner submitting multiple concurrent remote-agent pods: remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime each call createAgent() independently; if they overlap in time, they compete for the same limited vm slots.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the identical scheduling error, confirming the entire feature's eval surface is blocked by the shared infrastructure dependency.

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the production cluster immediately to determine if the resource is still exhausted or has since freed up.
Identify and review any long-running or leaked remote-agent pods that may be holding vm slots without active workloads, and terminate them if safe to do so.

Assess whether the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have sufficient capacity for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads; if not, evaluate adding more nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource label.

Review whether the three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are submitted concurrently during a single eval run, and if so, consider serializing them to reduce peak vm slot demand.

Confirm whether this is an eval-only infrastructure issue or whether real remote-agent provisioning requests from users are also failing — no user-traffic signals are present in this packet, so that determination requires separate incident or traffic data.
After cluster capacity is confirmed available, re-run the full remote-agents eval suite to verify all three checks pass and collect the expected evidence fields.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) share the identical failure message. Confirming the shared createAgent() call path is the single point of failure rules out independent per-check defects.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl node describe showing kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > 0 and Requests = 0 on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause.
A successful remote-agent pod scheduling event in cluster logs at the same timestamp would indicate the scheduler message was transient or from a different pod, not the eval pod.

A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime with full evidence collected would indicate the scheduling issue has resolved and was not a persistent capacity problem.

Evidence that the 4 non-kata nodes were temporarily cordoned or had a different affinity mismatch unrelated to the kata.peerpods.io/vm label would shift the cause toward a node configuration change rather than resource exhaustion.
Cluster event logs showing the eval pod was scheduled but the agent process itself crashed before returning evidence would indicate an application-layer failure rather than a scheduling failure.
followUpEvals: Add a preflight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all eligible nodes before submitting remote-agent pods, and fails fast with a clear capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting 143 s for the scheduler timeout.

Add a cluster-node-capacity eval that monitors the ratio of used-to-allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and emits a warning when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add a remote-agent pod scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a test pod and warns if it exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30 s), catching degraded scheduling before it causes full eval timeouts.

Add a remote-agents eval that checks for Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable age (e.g., 60 s) and surfaces them as a warning, enabling faster detection of scheduling stalls between full eval runs.
